title: OneNote: Copilot Notebooks suggest artifacts to create
summary: The briefing passes: the rollout, default availability, licensing statements and documented controls are supported. The Cloud Policy path is documented across the two cited policy pages, and the briefing preserves the tenant-only restriction on the preview Graph API and the distinction between current and legacy storage.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path is Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Create and view Copilot Pages and Copilot Notebooks.
claims.quote:
Under **Customization**, select **Policy Management**.
On the **Policy configurations** page, select **Create**.
On the **Start with the basics** page, enter a name (required) and a description (optional), then select **Next**.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors is the documented Graph route for applying a configuration baseline once.
claims.quote:
applies a desired-state baseline once in `applyOnce` mode.
POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors

claims.claim: The Graph request uses mode applyOnce and a baseline containing resources and their properties.
claims.quote: | mode | monitorMode | The monitor mode. The possible values are: `monitorOnly`, `applyOnce`, `unknownFutureValue`. Optional; defaults to `monitorOnly`. |

claims.claim: For microsoft.copilot.copilotpagesnotebooks, the resource's properties.value string is "0" to disable and "1" to enable.
The Tenant Configuration Management Graph API is preview.
claims.quote: This article lists the Copilot resource types supported in preview for monitoring and snapshots through the Tenant Configuration Management (TCM) APIs in Microsoft Graph beta.

claims.claim: The Graph route supports these Copilot settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.
claims.quote: The 20 Copilot resources are Office Cloud Policy Service (OCPS) settings. TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: The Graph operations fail for a target setting configured in a group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and `applyOnce` fail for that resource.

claims.claim: Licences are assigned through Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote:
In the admin center, go to the **Billing** > [Licenses](https://go.microsoft.com/fwlink/p/?linkid=842264) page.
Select a product.
On the product details page, select **Assign licenses**.

claims.claim: Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @() assigns a product licence to a user.
claims.quote:
To assign a license to a user, use the following command in PowerShell.
Set-MgUserLicense -UserId $userUPN -AddLicenses @{SkuId = "<SkuId>"} -RemoveLicenses @()

claims.claim: When several applicable group policies conflict, the highest-priority Cloud Policy setting applies.
claims.quote: If the user is a member of multiple Microsoft Entra groups with conflicting policy settings, priority is used to determine which policy setting is applied. The highest priority is applied, with "0" being the highest priority that you can assign.

claims.claim: A Cloud Policy change can take up to 90 minutes to be reflected when policy configurations already existed.
claims.quote: If there were existing policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 90 minutes to be reflected.

claims.claim: A Cloud Policy change can take up to 24 hours to be reflected when no policy configurations previously existed.
claims.quote: If there were no policy configurations before the change, the change takes up to 24 hours to be reflected.
